newsitem.title: UK: New drink promoted as "Michael Jackson's official drink".
newsitem.headline: New drink promoted as "Michael Jackson's official drink".

text.p: A new beverage called "Mystery" and described as pop star Michael Jackson's official drink is being promoted across Europe, the company involved said on Monday.
Mystery, billed as "an isotonic mineral beverage," is being introduced throughout the region as part of Jackson's History concert tour.
"It is the official Michael Jackson drink," Bernhard Hummel, assistant managing director of Mystery Drinks GmbH, told Reuters on Monday.

The peach-flavoured beverage is the brainchild of Karl Neubacher, managing director of Mystery Drinks. Neubacher approached Jackson's record label, Sony International, and Jackson's own company with the idea and won approval to launch Mystery as Jackson's official drink, Hummel said.
"Mystery is different because it's not a beverage like Coke or Pepsi," Hummel said in a phone interview from Mystery Drinks' headquarters in Frankfurt. "It's supposed to be a merchandising article."
Mystery is packaged in a slim, gold-coloured can featuring a picture of a bronze statue of Michael Jackson draped with bandoliers.
The beverage is described as "fresh, cool, magic".
In addititon to the beverage, Mystery Drinks is selling a related line of merchandise, including leather jackets and baseball caps.

The drink was initially introduced in Amsterdam last September during Jackson's concert engagement there and in the last two months has been introduced in Germany, Austria, Spain and Switzerland under licence agreements with local distributors.
It is to be launched in Britain next summer in conjunction with Jackson's concert dates here. Mystery Drinks is also forming ventures to introduce the beverage in the Middle East and Southeast Asia.
"We intend to obtain licencees all over the world," Hummel said.
Mystery is being distributed in Germany by Rewe Handelsgruppe AG, the privately held supermarket giant. The beverage in Germany is being sold for 2.49 marks ($1.46) per can.
The beverage has sales to date of six million units, including 1.5 million in Germany.

"We hope we can make it famous through the concerts," Hummel said. The beverage is being promoted on a German satellite television channel, SatOne, and was introduced in Spain with a billboard advertising campaign.
